subject: Reserved GPU capacity: scaling plan & SLA options for OrionAI chat (throughput/discount proposal)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@orionai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Reserved GPU capacity sizing — initial ask and files attached

Hi Sarah,

Great to chat yesterday — as promised, I'm following up with a concrete ask so we can align on a recommended Dedicated (reserved) GPU pool configuration and a preliminary pricing band. I attached a small sample of your request logs (orionai_qps_sample.csv) — thanks for sending that over.

Quick summary of OrionAI's production workload (please correct me if any of these are off):
- Peak concurrent users: ~10k active chats (peak hour)
- Average requests per minute (steady state): 2,400 rpm
- Peak requests per minute (burst): 7,800 rpm (spiky events)
- Typical prompt length: 180 tokens user + 220 tokens system/context = ~400 tokens input
- Average generated output: 160 tokens
- Typical session concurrency per model: 1.8 (many short interactions)
- Target latency P95: <= 250ms for streaming token start, <= 800ms full response for 512-token outputs

Key asks from OrionAI we discussed: throughput guarantees during product launches, a predictable monthly committed price with a 12–18 month reserved term, and the ability to burst to additional capacity for a short window (24–48 hours) with known cost.

Can you confirm the workload numbers above and attach any extra telemetry (percentile sequence-length histogram) you can share? Once I have that, we (Marissa and Karthik) will size a recommended GPU pool and send back a pricing/commit proposal and a draft SLA for review.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm telemetry and add any missing payload shapes (images/long context sessions).
2) We send a recommended pool configuration with sizing logic and price bands (reserved commit + burst pricing).
3) Align on contract term and SLA (Marissa will suggest a canary rollout plan for the first month).

Thanks — happy to jump on another 30-min call if that's easier.

Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: orionai_qps_sample.csv (CSV, 120KB)

From: Sarah Lin <sarah@orionai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@orionai.com
Date: 2026-12-05T13:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Reserved GPU capacity sizing — initial ask and files attached

Ben — thanks, this looks right. A few clarifications from the ops team:
- The 7,800 rpm burst is usually a 20–40 minute event during marketing pushes; sustained bursts above 5k rpm happen ~3x/month.
- We occasionally have longer contexts for multi-turn sessions (up to 1,200 tokens input + 800 tokens generation) but that's <5% of traffic.
- We need an explicit fallback policy: if reserved pool is saturated, requests should failover to a lower-cost hosted model we can pay for on-demand (acceptable for non-critical traffic).

We're interested in a 12-month reserved commit but want an option to scale up at month 6 if traffic trends make sense. Also we'll need SOC2 evidence and audit logs as part of procurement.

I'll loop in procurement if you send a draft commitment + SLA.

—Sarah
Sarah Lin | Head of Platform, OrionAI
sarah@orionai.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-06T08:21:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Reserved GPU capacity sizing — Orion clarifications / action items

Marissa / Karthik — FYI, Orion confirmed burst profile and asked for a 12-month commit with a scale-up option at month 6. They also require SOC2 evidence and an audit-log export for procurement.

Please see my rough notes on what I think they need and a couple of options to present:
A) Conservative (cost-focused):
 - Pool: 4x A100-80GB (sharded across 4 nodes)
 - Expected steady-state throughput: ~2.2k rpm at p95 latency target (with caching / prefix deduping)
 - Burst strategy: on-demand hosted fallback + 24-hour on-call burst pool (manual scaling)
 - Monthly commit: 40% discount over hosted list price; no guaranteed burst SLA

B) Performance (SLA-focused):
 - Pool: 8x A100-80GB (or 8x equivalent Ampere family GPUs with larger aggregate memory)
 - Expected steady-state throughput: ~6.5k rpm with headroom for 8k short bursts, p95 latency goals met for 512-token responses
 - Burst strategy: automated cross-region overflow and reserved burst nodes (24–48 hour burst capacity guaranteed)
 - Monthly commit: 55% discount, includes 4 guaranteed burst hours per incident, 99.95% uptime SLA, and rollback plan

Pricing notion: commit tiers priced as monthly flat + per-token overage if usage exceeds commit. We should prepare a rollback credit schedule and an early-termination clause that aligns with sales practice.

Can you run quick thumb calculations on GPU efficiency assumptions (tokens/sec per GPU for their token distributions) and build a short Excel we can send back with a recommended fallback and pricing band? I'll draft the email to Sarah once you confirm the numbers.

-Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-07T10:45:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Reserved GPU capacity sizing — Orion clarifications / action items

Ben — ran the sizing with Karthik's kern perf estimates and Orion's sequence histogram. Key assumptions (call out):
- Model variant: fp16 / q4_8 quantized variant we expect to serve (similar to 13B dense performance).
- Average end-to-end token throughput per A100-80GB (steady-state, with batching & KV cache): ~2,100 generated tokens/sec (for 400-token requests, streaming enabled).
- Effective concurrency handling: 24 concurrent sessions per GPU for target latency at 400-token context; longer contexts reduce parallelism to ~10 sessions/GPU at 1,200-token context.

Sizing results:
- Conservative (Option A): 4 GPUs -> estimated steady peak handled = ~2,100 rpm (note: this falls short of Orion's steady state of 2.4k rpm; would require additional optimizations such as request shaping or more cache TTL).
- Mid (recommended balanced): 6 GPUs -> estimated steady peak = ~3,150 rpm, burst headroom to ~5k rpm for 30–45 min with degraded p95 but acceptable fallbacks.
- Performance (Option B): 9 GPUs -> estimated steady peak = ~4,725 rpm, comfortable headroom for 8k rpm short bursts with reserved burst nodes activated (suggest 2 hot spare GPUs to handle spikes).

Pricing sketch (monthly committed cost, USD):
- 4 GPU commit: $68,000/mo (40% off hosted list), overage per token at hosted rate
- 6 GPU commit: $98,000/mo (48% off hosted list), includes 8 hours/month guaranteed burst capacity (automatic), 99.9% uptime SLA
- 9 GPU commit: $140,000/mo (55% off hosted list), includes 24 hours/month guaranteed burst capacity, 99.95% uptime SLA, 2 hot spare GPUs for rapid scaling

Recommended sales position: present the 6-GPU plan as the primary recommendation — it addresses their steady-state need, offers automated burst headroom, and keeps the commit size flexible. Include an explicit scale-up option at month 6 (pricing to be recalculated when they show sustained growth for 60 days).

I'll attach a short Excel with the per-GPU token/sec math and a draft SLA for Ben to send.

Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: commit_pricing_summary.xlsx, SLA_Draft_Redwood_v1.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@orionai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-09T16:22:00-08:00
Subject: Proposed reserved-commit offer & next steps (OrionAI)

Sarah — thanks for the context and for confirming the burst profile. Based on Orion's telemetry and Marissa's sizing, here's a clean offer and the immediate next steps.

Offer (12-month reserved commit, month-to-month billing options available on signature):
- Recommended: 6x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs (balanced plan)
  • Handles ~3.1k rpm steady state with automated headroom for ~5k rpm short bursts
  • Monthly commit: $98,000 (48% off hosted list for the selected model family)
  • Includes: 8 guaranteed burst hours/month (automatic scale), SOC2 evidence bundle, audit-log exports, and onboarding support (2-week canary roll)
- Upsell / higher SLA: 9x GPUs at $140,000/mo (55% off) for 24 guaranteed burst hours/mo and 99.95% SLA

Contract mechanics:
- Early scale option at month 6: customer can request a one-way scale-up; pricing is repriced pro-rata based on the new commit (we'll provide a 10-day notice path for billing changes).
- Overages: usage beyond commit billed at hosted list per-token rate; we can also offer a blended overage rate as a middle ground.
- Credits: we propose a rollback credit schedule tied to availability (outlined in the attached SLA draft).

Next steps:
1) If this looks good, sign a short mutual action plan and we'll send a redline-friendly SOW + DocuSign link. (HubSpot link to the deal is attached.)
2) Procurement: we'll provide a SOC2 pack and the audit-log export process.
3) Tech kickoff: Marissa will run the canary rollout plan and confirm the burst automation configuration.

Attached: commit_pricing_summary.xlsx (breakdown), SLA_Draft_Redwood_v1.pdf (draft).

If you'd like, we can hold a call tomorrow to walk the team through the canary and burst behavior.

Best,
Ben
